newsitem.title: GHANA: Ashanti pulls Ghana Stock Exchange down.
newsitem.headline: Ashanti pulls Ghana Stock Exchange down.

text.p: Blue chips tumbled in trading on the Ghana Stock Exchange on Friday after a big drop in Ashanti Goldfields Ltd shares weighed down on the market.
Ashanti fell 1,000 cedis to 21,000 cedis followed by Mobil Oil Ghana Ltd, down 200 cedis to 5,300 cedis. The lone gainer, Social Security Bank closed 12 cedis better at 1,080 cedis.
As a result the GSE All-Share Index recorded one of its biggest declines for a trading session, dropping 2.25 points to 357.94 points.
One trader said sentiment on the bourse where Ashanti is the weightiest stock was overcast with uncertainty over the price of gold following a dramatic new year slide on world markets.
"I think we are nearing a bottomline around $355 an ounce," the trader said.
Gold was fixed in London at $358.25 per ounce on Friday.
In a reasonably active session, total share offers closed at 3,846,120 to bids of 2,703,020 with a moderate 749,770 shares changing hands. ($=1,730)
